title: Lil Cosign Tells All
teaser: He was in the booth, in the studio and in the car outside. Now he's talking.

news.headline: In the Booth
news.body: Lil Cosign, Lord Menace's hype man, was at Velvet Static the night of the photo. He says the King of Steinway Street had a very specific problem: the door.
news.hook: Cosign: "She told him exactly when to post. Down to the minute."
news.post:
Roommates, every rapper has a hype man, and every hype man has seen things. Lord Menace's is Lil Cosign: twenty-six, from Rego Park, real name withheld because he begged. He's agreed to tell me everything, one piece at a time, in exchange for a shoutout and a chopped cheese. Bet.

He starts with the booth.

"The night he took that photo, we pulled up to Velvet Static around eleven," Cosign told me. "And yo, the guy at the door looked at him one time, and he got behind me. Behind ME. I'm five-foot-six."

The King of Steinway Street, y'all, hiding behind a five-foot-six hype man because somebody at a door looked at him. Not him saying in a song last year that he "fears nothing but God and taxes." He forgot doors.

"Toni was already in the booth. The corner one. She said it was her favorite. She told him to sit on the left, because 'the light's better on my right.'"

Then the photo. Cosign says Toni took it herself: three angles, picked one, handed back the phone. "Then she goes, 'Post it tomorrow at 4:12.' Not 4. Not 4:15. 4:12. He asked why. She said, 'Trust the process.'"

He posted at 4:12. Fifty minutes later, Big Ruckus posted her in the same booth. "I thought he was gonna faint," Cosign said. "He sat on the floor of his mom's kitchen for an hour. Then he called me: 'We gotta drop something tonight.' I said, B, we don't have anything. He said, 'We have the tow receipt.'"

Wait. Where did he get Ruckus's tow receipt? "Somebody sent it to him. A message. He didn't say who. He was too hype to tell me."

And the retainer from Ruckus's diss? "Real. He sleeps in it. He calls it 'the night guard.' It is not a night guard."

Cosign also wants it on the record that he wrote the best line on "Rental Car Ruckus" and got no credit. Which line? "The one that goes 'skrrt.'" Respect, I guess.

So tell me, Roommates: what's the most embarrassing thing your best friend could tell the internet about you? And who sends a man somebody else's tow receipt?

news.headline: Take Forty-One
news.body: The "Rental Car Ruckus" session took forty-one takes. Lil Cosign was there for every one, and he has notes, plus thoughts on suing Sal.
news.hook: Take 38 was ruined by a call from a dentist's office. Guess whose.
news.post:
Roommates, Lil Cosign is back, and today he's taking us into the studio. Not a fancy one. A basement in Rego Park with egg-crate foam on the walls and a mini fridge that only holds seltzer.

"Rental Car Ruckus" sounds like it was made in one angry take. It was not. "Forty-one takes," Cosign told me. "Forty-one. He kept saying 'hydrogen' instead of 'hydrant.' Like, 'you got towed from a hydrogen.' Bro. That's the sun."

Takes 1 to 12: hydrogen. Takes 13 to 20: he got the word right but asked Cosign if the second verse was "too mean." Cosign: "It's a diss track. Mean is the whole job." Takes 21 to 37: they changed "your car's a joke" to "your car's a rental," because Menace said jokes "can hurt people." Take 38: his phone rang mid-verse. The caller ID said "Dr. Pettibone's Office." It was a reminder about his cleaning. "He answered," Cosign said. "In the booth. On the mic. He said, 'Yes, Thursday works.'"

Chile. That's on the session file forever.

Take 41 is the one you heard. Cosign's ad-libs are in it: "SKRRT," "TOWED!" and, at 1:12, very quietly, "sorry." Nobody else noticed. Now you will.

Then the lawsuit. Cosign was not on board. "I told him, B, don't sue Sal. Everybody loves Sal. The cat loves Sal. He said, 'It's my brand.' I said, what brand? The brand is egg whites."

Here's the part that got me. Cosign gets paid in sandwiches. Literally. Lord Menace covers his breakfast at Sal's every day as "hype man compensation." Which means for the last two years, Cosign has been ordering "The Lord Menace" too. "It's not bad," he said. "It's not good either. It's like eating a cloud that's mad at you."

When "Retainer" dropped forty minutes after their track, Cosign says Menace listened to it in the studio, alone, three times, in total silence. Then he turned around and asked, "Does it sound like I sleep in it?"

So tell me, Roommates: how many takes would it take you to say "hydrant"? And would you work for egg whites?

news.headline: The Name
news.body: Lil Cosign has known Lord Menace's real name since seventh grade and never said it once. Then the courthouse steps happened, and then the radio did.
news.hook: Cosign: "I'm the only one who ever called him Des. Now everybody does."
news.post:
Roommates, the whole borough learned the name Desmond Pettibone yesterday. Lil Cosign learned it in seventh grade.

"We met in band class," he told me. "He played triangle. I played the other triangle. We were the triangle section." Not the King of Steinway Street having a triangle origin story while his rival had an oboe. Queens is a small town with tall buildings.

Cosign says he has never said "Desmond" out loud in public. Not once in fourteen years. "That was the deal. He's Menace outside. He's Des at his mom's. I kept that sacred." Then yesterday a lawyer said it into a microphone with a jingle playing, and the whole thing was over in four seconds.

Cosign drove him home from the deposition. "He laid down in the back seat under his coat. The whole ride. At a red light a kid on a scooter looked in and said, 'Yo, is that Pettibone?' He said, 'No.' From under the coat."

At his mom's house, Dr. Pettibone made him chamomile and told him, "Desmond is a beautiful name. I picked it." Cosign says Menace cried. "Not a lot. A respectful amount."

Then this morning, Toni's radio interview. Cosign and Menace listened in the car outside a jeweler on Steinway Street. When Toni said, "I love Desmond in a very special way," Menace grabbed Cosign's arm and said, "You hear that? Special." Then she said the exact same thing about Gerald. "I said, bro, she said it twice. Word for word. He said, 'Mine was more special.'"

Then they went inside, and Menace bought the C$40,000 diamond phone case. Cosign says the jeweler looked at the receipt, laughed and said, "Two in one day! What a week!" Menace thought he meant two great customers. Cosign didn't say anything. "I should've said something," he told me. "I didn't say something."

My inbox is wildin', because a lot of y'all have a Des in your life too.

So tell me, Roommates: would you keep your best friend's real name a secret for fourteen years? And what would you have said to that jeweler?

news.headline: The Parking Lot
news.body: While two rappers hid in one restroom, their hype men were stuck downstairs with the engines running. Lil Cosign met Big Ruckus's hype man, and they figured it out first.
news.hook: Cosign: "She asked me for his mom's office number. Weeks ago. I gave it to her. That's on me."
news.post:
Roommates, everybody's talking about the restroom. Nobody's talking about the parking lot. Lil Cosign was in the parking lot.

"I dropped him at the Ditmars Heights Rooftop at nine," Cosign told me. "He had two dozen roses and his good coat. I'm waiting in the car. Then this lime-green car pulls up next to me, and out comes Big Ruckus with two dozen roses. And then out comes his hype man."

Big Ruckus's hype man is called Tiny Thunder. He is six-foot-seven. He brought Princess Biscuit, who rode in a carrier on the passenger seat with her own seat belt.

For forty-five minutes, while their bosses hid in a single-stall restroom upstairs, the two hype men stood between their cars and did not speak. Then Tiny Thunder opened a family-size bag of chips and held it out. Cosign took one. "And that was it. Peace talks."

They started comparing notes. Tiny Thunder said Toni once asked him, very casually, where Gerald keeps "that cute little instrument case." He told her: under the bed. Cosign went quiet. Then he said Toni once asked him for Dr. Pettibone's office number, "to book a whitening." He gave it to her.

"We just looked at each other," Cosign said. "Like, oh. OH. She asked both of us one little thing. One little question each. And that's all it took."

At 9:47 their bosses came out, no roses, faces gray, and got in the cars without a word. On the ride home, at a red light on Ditmars, Menace asked, "Did you know?" Cosign told me what he said, and I'm printing it exactly: "I knew a little. I knew one tooth's worth."

Not the hype men solving the case before the rappers did, with a bag of chips and a Pomeranian as a witness. We love to see the support staff win.

Cosign and Tiny Thunder have a group chat now. It's called "the lot." Mad wholesome.

So tell me, Roommates: what's the one little thing you told somebody that you wish you could take back?

news.headline: Hype Man for an Oboe
news.body: Desmond & Gerald have an acoustic duo, a ballad and a hype man. Lil Cosign explains his broken heart, sandwich and question mark, and starts his new job.
news.hook: Cosign's new job title: "tambourine, emotional support, merch."
news.post:
Roommates, for our last chat, Lil Cosign met me at the slice shop, because Sal's is "too emotional right now." Respect.

First, the post. When Toni confessed yesterday, Cosign posted three emojis and nothing else: a broken heart, a sandwich and a question mark. The internet spent a whole day decoding it. Here's the official translation, straight from the man. "Broken heart: Des. Sandwich: Sal knew the whole time. Question mark: what do I do now?"

He has an answer now. Desmond & Gerald, the acoustic duo nobody ordered, have a hype man. Two, actually. Cosign and Tiny Thunder are splitting the job. Their first gig was an open mic this afternoon, a guitar, an oboe and a ballad called "We Got Played," and Cosign stood at the side of the stage with a tambourine, shouting the softest ad-libs in New York history. "YEAH! FEELINGS!" "SAY THAT AGAIN, GERALD!" "THAT'S GROWTH!"

His business cards already say "tambourine, emotional support, merch." The merch is a hoodie that says "WE GOT PLAYED" on the front and "AND WE GREW" on the back. It's selling. Not as well as the PETTIBONE ones, but it's selling.

I asked him how Des is really doing. "Honestly? Better. He's eating salt again. A little. On eggs. Gerald's teaching him the oboe. It sounds like a goose. But a happy goose."

And Toni? Cosign isn't mad. "She played us. Facts. But she played us so good, the song's number one, and we're number nine, and Des and Gerald are friends now. That's not losing. That's a weird kind of winning."

One more thing, he said, and his face got serious. "Toni thanked a lot of people this week. I checked. I wasn't on it." He took a bite of his slice. "I'm on Des's list, though. That's the list that matters."

Roommates, I came for tea and I left with a lump in my throat and grease on my sleeve. Cheesin', for real.

So tell me, one last time: who's the Lil Cosign in your life? And would you play tambourine for your best friend's oboe?
